note:
CASH & CARRION — the Marrow Street fence, and the building the authored pass started from.

It was `In Hock We Trust` on the `pawn` arm: four stacked boxes of alternating half-width, which
produced a wedding cake of projecting ledges with a billboard on stilts over it. The first rewrite
fixed the name and the materials and left the proportions alone, and the proportions were the half
that was still wrong.

The name says the trade — you bring it in, they give you cash, and what they buy is what somebody
else is finished with — and the building says it too: granite you can't kick in, a brass fascia, a
roller shutter, barred windows and the three gilt balls that have meant pawnbroker for seven
hundred years.

⚠ IT IS FOUR STOREYS, AND THE FLOOR COUNT WAS THE BUG. `TYPE_FLOORS.fence` is 2, the tile carried
no override, and every neighbour on this stretch of Marrow Street is three or four — so it drew to
0.052 world-z against Co-Pay & Pray's 0.103 next door and read as a bungalow between two blocks.
Nothing in this file could have fixed that: every `z` here is a fraction of `h`, so the whole model
scales together and a taller one is the same squat building drawn bigger. `flags.floors: 4` on
zone_district_916_910 is the fix, and the proportions below are authored against it — a tall
trading hall, then three shorter storeys over it, which is the right way round for the type.

⚠ THE THREE BALLS ARE MASS, NOT LIGHTS. The arm hung them as `blinkLight`s, so by daylight the
trade sign on a pawnbroker was invisible, which is the one hour of the day it most needs to be
read. They are three brass drums with a warm light AT each of them, so they read as objects by day
and as lamps after dark. They sit two-over-one, which is the arrangement the symbol actually has.

⚠ AND A BALL IS TALLER IN AUTHORED UNITS THAN IT LOOKS. The projection draws world-z and world-plan
at about the same scale (`depth / FL` ≈ 0.87 at the sim's aspect), but an authored `h` unit is
worth about 0.77 of an authored `fh` unit on this tile — so a drum authored round comes out a
pancake. The old set spanned 0.046 in z against a radius of 0.03 and read as three brass pucks on a
band. These span 0.090, which is `2.3 × r` carried through the basis.

⚠ THE STEP UP IS IN THE MIDDLE AND IT IS STONE. The old arm stepped IN — each box narrower than the
one under it — which is what made it a stack of shelves. Here a projecting centre bay rises through
the shaft, breaks the cornice and is capped in bronze, so the silhouette has one event in it and
the name is cut where a building of this kind would cut it.

The signs are a ladder rather than copies of one another: the name across the fascia at eye
level, H. HOCK cut into the crest. The Chinese trade word is the derived kit's blade and the
roof hoarding is the kit's too, so nothing up there is authored here — an authored crest board
saying CASH & CARRION under the kit's hoarding saying CASH & CARRION was the old wedding cake
in signage, and the kit already carries `$name` for any building that does not sign its own roof.

⚠ AN AUTHORED glowPool HAS NO NIGHT TERM. `AUTHORED_ADORN` hands it `c.alpha` and nothing else,
where neonBlade, marqueeBand, awning and roofCross all take `c.night` — so a glow sized to read
as a lamp after dark is a hot core painted over the brass at noon, and the three balls came out
as three lit panels. Every glow here is smaller than the thing it sits on.
